locator.section: 8 Detailed Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Eq. 8.46, two-step path: i-cleavage of the oxocarbenium)

evidence.curator_note: Second stage of the two-step path in Eq. 8.46: inductive (i) cleavage of the even-electron oxocarbenium C6H13-O(+)=CH2 (m/z 115) losing neutral formaldehyde O=CH2 to give the n-hexyl cation C6H13(+) (m/z 85). The charge site draws the C7-O1 bonding pair onto oxygen; the C7-O1 sigma bond breaks heterolytically and the surviving O1=C2 double bond becomes neutral formaldehyde. Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs: the vertical 'i' pathway arrow between the m/z-115 and m/z-77% species carries the neutral loss '-O=CH2'; no curved arrow is drawn. The text calls this the 'two-step pathway' to the same m/z-85 ion. Encoded as ONE double-barbed (2-electron) heterolytic arrow onto O1; the validator's soft 'lone pair rather than radicals' note on atom 1 is expected (the arriving pair is a lone pair completing formaldehyde's carbonyl oxygen).

evidence.curator_note: No MØD rule is cross-linked: rule_index.json has no by_equation entry for 8.46. The precursor here is the m/z-115 oxocarbenium FRAGMENT ion (adduct null, not the [M]+. molecular ion); precursor_mz 115.1112 is its curator-computed monoisotopic value. The product C6H13+ (m/z 85.1006) is the SAME peak as in IMS8-EQ8.46b (relative_intensity 0.77 is the combined 70 eV EI abundance of C6H13+ from both the one-step i-cleavage and this two-step route). ms_context activation is consecutive 70 eV EI source fragmentation, NOT a CAD/MI experiment.

ms_context.activation_method: 70 eV EI (consecutive source fragmentation of the m/z-115 oxocarbenium)
